discrepancies.note: Discrepancy: no 'Notes' heading exists anywhere in the source. The footnotes sit at the bottom of page 1 with no heading text; the rebuild's h2 'Notes' is a synthesized section title for the relocated footnotes, and the HTML renders no review note disclosing the addition.

Discrepancy: source page 1 carries three internal link annotations on the superscript footnote markers [1][2][3] (GoTo links jumping to the footnotes); in the rebuild these markers are plain text with no anchors linking to the relocated Notes section. The blank page image (image-001-obj74.png, 888x157 DeviceGray, renders solid white) was also dropped. Neither is disclosed - the HTML contains no review-notes section. All running text, both external links, both emails, the letterhead image, and the signature block are present.

Discrepancy: the h2 'Notes' is document content that does not exist anywhere in the source and is undisclosed. All other additions are standard accessibility scaffolding (skip link, page-break marker labeled 'Page 2', meta description) rather than document content; body text otherwise matches the source with no invented sentences.

Discrepancy on the disclosure clause: the linear order itself is an improvement (letterhead, date, salutation, body with the page-1/page-2 straddling sentence rejoined, signature block, then footnotes last), but the relocation of footnotes 1-3 from the bottom of page 1 to an end-of-document Notes section after the page-2 signature is nowhere disclosed - the rebuilt HTML renders no review notes.

Discrepancy: the rebuilt HTML contains no review-notes section at all, so none of the observed transformations are disclosed: footnotes 1-3 relocated under a synthesized 'Notes' h2; footnote-marker internal links dropped (plain [1][2][3] text); the cross-page sentence rejoined with page-2 text inside a paragraph tagged data-source-page="1"; the blank image obj74 omitted; and the metadata title's trailing ' (PDF)' trimmed from the h1.

meaning: 'verified' means an independent reader attested every item against the source. It does not upgrade any compliance claim, and the script cannot prove the reader's independence - it records the attestation.

verifier.statement: I read source.pdf directly via pdfjs: reading-order per-page lines (extract_pages.cjs / pages-ordered.json), the raw object-order text layer, italic-face evidence (extract_f3.cjs: TimesNewRomanPS-ItalicMT items on page 1, roman-only page 2), embedded metadata Title (meta.cjs), and link annotations on both pages via a page.getAnnotations() script I wrote (check_annots.cjs); I viewed both extracted images (image-002-obj75.jpg letterhead, image-001-obj74.png blank) with the Read tool, then read alloflow-output/source-accessible.html in full (all 76 lines, which render no review-notes section) and compared it block by block against the source. I did not read repair-plan.json or any other notes.
